newsitem.title: USA: NBA-AFTER DUNCAN, REST OF WEDNESDAY'S DRAFT A MYSTERY.
newsitem.headline: NBA-AFTER DUNCAN, REST OF WEDNESDAY'S DRAFT A MYSTERY.

text.p: The San Antonio Spurs are sure to take Wake Forest centre Tim Duncan with the number one pick in Wednesday night's NBA Draft, but after that it's a guessing game as to which players go where.

Ten years after selecting centre David Robinson with the first overall pick, the Spurs will again land the best player in college basketball this year when they welcome aboard Duncan at the draft staged at the Charlotte Coliseum.
"I feel very lucky," said Duncan, who will be the first senior chosen with the top pick since Larry Johnson in 1991.

"I think that stepping into a situation where we can go out and win games our first year, I'm really happy about that. Playing with David (Robinson) and being able to learn from him will be a great opportunity for me."

As clearly as Duncan is the best player available, the remainder of the draft is a muddled mystery. The next five teams all have expressed interest in trading their picks -- either to move up to get someone they covet, or to move down to save some money.

The Philadelphia 76ers pick second and are reportedly considering three players. New 76ers coach Larry Brown appears to have narrowed it down to Texas Tech centre Tony Battie, Colorado guard Chauncey Billups or Utah forward Keith Van Horn.
But Billups and Van Horn have indicated they are not thrilled about the idea of playing for the Sixers, who lost 60 games last season.
The Boston Celtics own the third and sixth picks and offered both to San Antonio for the first pick. The Spurs rejected the offer.

The Celtics need help everywhere and new coach Rick Pitino is trying to acquire an impact player in return for the picks. Pitino has said the Celtics would use the third pick on Billups, Van Horn or Battie.
The Vancouver Grizzlies pick fourth and the Denver Nuggets have the fifth selection. The Grizzlies appear to be targeting guard Antonio Daniels of Bowling Green.
A record 40 players left school early for the draft, including high schooler Tracy McGrady, who figures to go high.
The Celts may opt for McGrady, who will be the fourth high schooler taken in the first round in the last three years, with their second first-round pick.

Pitino also could opt for Kentucky forward Ron Mercer, whom he has said is the best athlete he has ever coached. That would reunite Mercer with Pitino and Antoine Walker, the key elements of Kentucky's 1996 college championship team.
Regardless of what happens in the first six picks, forward Tim Thomas of Villanova -- who played just one year of college ball -- should be available to the New Jersey Nets, who pick seventh.
The Celtics are among three teams with two first-round picks. The others are the Cleveland Cavaliers (13th and 16th) and the Nets, who also select 21st.
In addition to the host Charlotte Hornets, the Washington Wizards, Los Angeles Lakers and Phoenix Suns are without a first-round selection.
